cohort: The study included 104 patients with multifetal pregnancies (103 twin and 1 triplet) who either aborted or delivered at a tertiary care centre over an 18-month period.
finding: Multifetal pregnancies are associated with a high incidence of LSCS, preterm delivery, and a significant need for NICU care for the neonates, underscoring the necessity for management at a well-equipped tertiary care center.
mod_finding: Emergency LSCS was the most common mode of delivery (55.85%), followed by vaginal delivery for both babies (33.65%), with elective LSCS (3.8%) and instrumental delivery (1.9%) occurring less frequently.
followup_time: During hospital stay (antenatal, labor, and postnatal periods)
gest_age: Preterm delivery occurred in 78.8% of cases, with 75% delivering between 28-37 weeks, 10.6% delivering <28 weeks, and 14.4% delivering >37 weeks gestation.
